headline: Chip Rout Swamps the Tape as Just 106 of 663 Stocks Finish Higher
body_html:
Friday's session ended in broad retreat. Of the 663 stocks we track, 555 closed lower and only 106 closed higher. The dominant theme was a violent unwinding in semiconductors, which fell 10.01% as a group, far worse than any other corner of the market. The S&P 500 was reported to be heading for a sixth straight daily decline.

The damage reached well beyond chips. Financials lost 3.52%, energy 3.3%, and industrials and materials each gave up 3.15%. Software slipped 2.09% and healthcare 1.62%. Consumer names held up best among the decliners at down 1.37%. Homebuilders were the lone group in positive territory, up 0.34%, a modest tilt rather than a true bid.

The heaviest losses sat in component and hardware names. Applied Optoelectronics fell 16.55%, Celestica 16.07%, Sandisk 16.05%, Alpha and Omega Semiconductor 15.32% and Credo Technology 15.2%. Bloom Energy dropped 15.31%. Against that, Gap jumped 11.44% and was the session's standout, even after trimming its full-year outlook. Expectations matter as much as guidance. Monday's open will show whether the selling was exhaustion or the start of something longer.

briefs.headline: Gap Rallies Despite Lower Full-Year Outlook
briefs.body: Gap shares rose 11.44% on Friday, the best showing in our universe, even as the retailer lowered its full-year guidance. The company also named a new chief for its Athleta brand. The move suggests investors had already priced in a softer year.

briefs.headline: Apparel and Household Names Buck the Slide
briefs.body: The Buckle climbed 5.7% and Spectrum Brands gained 6.42%, adding to a consumer pocket that fell far less than the broader market. The consumer group closed down 1.37%, well ahead of the 3%-plus losses in financials, energy and industrials.

briefs.headline: Memory, Optical and Connectivity Names Lead the Chip Rout
briefs.body: Sandisk, Credo Technology and Alpha and Omega Semiconductor each lost more than 15%. Applied Optoelectronics fell 16.55%. With the semiconductor group down 10.01%, the selling was broad across memory, power and networking components, not confined to one niche.

briefs.headline: Fuel-Cell Maker Bloom Energy Sinks 15%
briefs.body: Bloom Energy fell 15.31%, the steepest drop among the energy names we track. The sector as a whole lost 3.3%. Friday's selling hit growth-oriented corners of the group hardest.

briefs.headline: Senate Republicans Block Iran War Resolution
briefs.body: Senate Republicans, backing the president, blocked a resolution on Iran military action. Separately, Trump said there is no rush to decide on Iran and pointed to next year. Western nations also pressed Iran at the IAEA to allow inspections at bombed nuclear sites.

briefs.headline: Heartflow Gains as Healthcare Slips
briefs.body: Heartflow rose 4.62%, one of the day's top gainers, while healthcare as a whole fell 1.62%. Sector news included Johnson & Johnson advancing two key products and Sanofi's prolonged Pompe drug shortage, which is leaving some patients struggling to access treatment.
